newsitem.title: INDIA: Truck movement through Bombay port at a standstill.
newsitem.headline: Truck movement through Bombay port at a standstill.

text.p: Movement of cargo by road in and out of Bombay port was at a standstill due to a truck strike across India, port manager R.D. Joshi told Reuters on Thursday.
He said dry cargo and container shipments were most affected, but there was still storage room for cargo to be held until the trucks start rolling again.
"We've got enough space and sheds are generally free," he said.
"There is not much congestion at all," he said.

Truck owners launched the strike on Tuesday in protest against a service tax and surge in insurance premiums. The protest began one day earlier around Bombay. An estimated 2.2 million trucks have been kept off the roads by the strike.
Joshi said four container ships were waiting, and four or five cargo vessels were waiting for export cargo to come.
He said there were enough berths available at the port to avoid loading and unloading delays once the truck strike was over.
But he expected clogged roads to hamper the flow of goods when the truckers restart their engines, and suggested that traffic control authorities should be prepared to smoothe the jams.
Discharge of oil and petroleum products at oil terminals were unaffected, he said.
